title: Work queues
summary: Move work off the request path when the user can wait for the result.

parts.rule: If the caller does not need the result in the same request, push that work onto a queue and return quickly.
parts.why: Long work on the request thread burns timeouts and hides retries. Queues make deferral explicit.
parts.example: SAMPLE: generating a preview image after upload enqueues a job; the upload response only stores the original and a pending flag.
parts.use: Use when latency budgets forbid inline heavy work and eventual completion is acceptable.
parts.refuse: Refuse a queue when the user must see the result before the response. Refuse confusing this with the data-structures queues slug.

body:
Rule. If the caller does not need the result in the same request, push that work onto a queue and return quickly.

Why it matters. Long work on the request thread burns timeouts and hides retries. Queues make deferral explicit.

SAMPLE example. SAMPLE: generating a preview image after upload enqueues a job; the upload response only stores the original and a pending flag.

When to use. Use when latency budgets forbid inline heavy work and eventual completion is acceptable.

When to refuse. Refuse a queue when the user must see the result before the response. Refuse confusing this with the data-structures queues slug.
